newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil cargoes lower on futures, barges up.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil cargoes lower on futures, barges up.

text.p: Outright NWE gas oil prices were mainly weaker on Thursday as IPE futures lost some of the recent gains to profit-taking, but premiums remained firm especially in the barge market where prompt supply was tight.
The IPE September contract was trading 50 cents off at $207.00 a tonne at 1114 GMT.

On the barge market, prices were fairly steady as tight prompt supply pushed up premiums. A prompt barge traded at Sept IPE +$4, fob ARA in early trade and by midday traders were quoting prompt premiums of Sept IPE +$4/+$5 fob ARA.
Prompt storage material was offered at Sept IPE +$4.

"The market's been pushed up by some short covering. Those who don't need material are staying out or concentrating on the second half," one trader said. Second half premiums were put at Sept IPE +$1.50/+$2 fob ARA.
On the cargo market, German heating oil cargoes were talked at Oct IPE +$$4.50/+$5. Traders said that heating oil was well supported by concerns over low stocks in the U.S. and Europe.
Traders said there was a fair amount of demand for low sulphur but buyers and sellers were in a stalemate situation over current premiums of Oct IPE +$16/+$18 cif NWE.
